shortDescription: Spain's manufacturing sector expanded in October at its fastest pace since August 2025 as output and new orders rose at the strongest rates in around a year, a business survey showed on Monday.

children: Spain's manufacturing sector expanded in October at its fastest pace since August 2025 as output and new orders rose at the strongest rates in around a year, a business survey showed on Monday.
The S&P Spain Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 52.2 in October from 51.0 in September. The 50 mark separates growth from contraction

"Spain's manufacturing sector showed some renewed resilience in the face of ongoing challenges during October. Production picked up and new orders increased for the first time in six months," said Paul Smith, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence
Production increased for a second straight month, while new orders rose at the strongest pace in 12 months. Export business also grew for a second month, helped by demand from key European markets
Backlogs of work rose at the fastest rate since August 2025. Employment slipped slightly as firms remained unwilling to replace leavers, adding to overall workloads

Supplier delivery times lengthened again in a deterioration that has continued since July 2023. Purchasing activity rose for the first time since last November, and stocks of purchases increased for the first time in 13 months

Input cost inflation accelerated to its strongest since May's four-year high, driven by energy, fuel, logistics and shipping costs. Output price inflation climbed to its highest since June as firms passed on higher expenses
Manufacturers remained optimistic about output over the coming year, although confidence fell from September to below trend as firms worried about rising costs and geopolitical uncertainty
